diff --git a/js/src/jit/MIROps.yaml b/js/src/jit/MIROps.yaml
index e13289224308..011bcc0b958b 100644
--- a/js/src/jit/MIROps.yaml
+++ b/js/src/jit/MIROps.yaml
@@ -2837,20 +2837,51 @@
 
 - name: StoreSlotByIteratorIndex
   operands:
     object: Object
     iterator: Object
     value: Value
   alias_set: custom
   generate_lir: true
   lir_temps: 2
 
+
+# The following two instructions need too many registers on x86. We could
+# spill or do some cheeky stuff potentially but it's likely not worth the
+# complexity
+#ifndef JS_CODEGEN_X86
+
+# Okay this is a confusing name, but essentially, the above ops load/store a
+# slot of an object using the PropertyIndex associated with the *current* key
+# for the iterator. The below op uses the PropertyIndex associated with the
+# key indexed by `index`, rather than the current one.
+- name: LoadSlotByIteratorIndexIndexed
+  operands:
+    object: Object
+    iterator: Object
+    index: Int32
+  result_type: Value
+  alias_set: custom
+  generate_lir: true
+  lir_temps: 2
+
+- name: StoreSlotByIteratorIndexIndexed
+  operands:
+    object: Object
+    iterator: Object
+    index: Int32
+    value: Value
+  alias_set: custom
+  generate_lir: true
+  lir_temps: 2
+#endif
+
 # Load the private value expando from a DOM proxy. The target is stored in the
 # proxy object's private slot.
 # This is either an UndefinedValue (no expando), ObjectValue (the expando
 # object), or PrivateValue(ExpandoAndGeneration*).
 - name: LoadDOMExpandoValue
   operands:
     proxy: Object
   result_type: Value
   movable: true
   congruent_to: if_operands_equal

fix_commit_message:
Bug 2003589 - Only enumerate own properties in Object.keys ObjToIterator r=iain

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D274985
agent_reasoning: Without this change, the shape/iterator cache can hand out the same NativeIterator to both a full (for-in style) enumeration and an Object.keys scalar-replacement enumeration. An Object.keys iterator built via the "unregistered" fast path only skips enumerator registration for GC/mutation invalidation bookkeeping — it did not otherwise restrict itself to own properties, and nothing stopped a full-enumeration iterator (whose keys may be able to include properties surfaced through a prototype, including a Proxy's own-keys trap) from being reused by the Object.keys path or vice versa. Since OptimizeIteratorIndices/LoadIteratorElement in Ion treat these iterators' cached indices as stable, direct, indexed slot accesses, an attacker could place a Proxy on the prototype chain whose trap runs arbitrary script during enumeration/reuse, invalidating the shapes/slots the JIT assumed were still valid and leading to out-of-bounds or type-confused access. Tagging Object.keys iterators as own-properties-only (via JSITER_OWNONLY and the new OwnPropertiesOnly/NotReusable flag) and refusing to let the two iterator flavors alias each other closes this gap: Object.keys iterators can never gain prototype-chain-derived entries, and a full iterator can never be mistaken for one eligible for the indices fast path's own-property-only guarantee.
